title: Turn the Right Dial
blurb: Text dials, image dials, deployment dials — match each symptom to the parameter that fixes it, past the near-miss the exam planted.
traps: Tune temperature OR top_p — not both

items.label: You need consistent, repeatable output from the same prompt every run
items.why: histack's exact exam cue: 'consistent, repeatable output' → low temperature. It rescales the whole probability distribution; tune it or top_p, not both.

items.label: Restrict sampling to the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a set threshold
items.why: Nucleus sampling — top_p truncates the candidate set, while temperature reshapes the whole distribution (corpus confused-pair #5).

items.label: Responses keep cutting off mid-sentence — you need complete answers
items.why: max_tokens caps output length only — the exam's most frequent parameter trap is offering it as a randomness control (pair #4).

items.label: The model keeps repeating one phrase; penalize tokens in proportion to how often they've appeared
items.why: Frequency penalty scales with repeat count (repetition); presence penalty fires once a token has appeared at all (topic novelty) — corpus pair #6.

items.label: Generated marketing images look rough — request the higher render fidelity tier
items.why: gpt-image-1's payload takes prompt, size, quality (including the 'high' trap value) and n — quality controls fidelity, size controls dimensions.

items.label: See image progress sooner while a large generation renders
items.why: Streaming partial_images on the images/generations path returns progressive output — the exam's 'see image progress sooner' stem verbatim.

items.label: The randomness knob that reshapes the entire token probability distribution before sampling, not just the top slice
items.why: Temperature scales logits across the whole distribution; top_p instead truncates by cumulative probability mass — same 'creativity' intuition, different mechanism.

items.label: The team wants the model to only ever consider the most probable slice of next-token candidates, cutting off the long tail
items.why: Nucleus sampling (top_p) restricts candidates to a cumulative-probability slice; temperature reshapes probabilities but never removes candidates outright.

items.label: A hard ceiling on how many tokens a single response can generate, regardless of what it says
items.why: max_tokens is a length ceiling enforced during generation; a stop sequence instead halts generation early only when a specific string appears — different trigger, same 'shorter output' goal.

items.label: Discourage the model from reusing the same word or phrase many times over — the more it repeats, the harder the pushback
items.why: Frequency penalty scales with how often a token has already appeared; presence penalty applies a flat penalty the moment a token appears even once — count-proportional vs binary.

items.label: The chat transcript never revisits earlier topics — the model always drifts onto new subject matter instead of returning to what it already covered
items.why: A high presence penalty fires the instant a token has appeared once, pushing the model toward new topics; frequency penalty scales with repeat count and mainly curbs literal repetition, not topic drift.

items.label: Applies the same fixed penalty to any token that has shown up at all in the response so far, no matter how many times
items.why: Presence penalty is binary per-token (appeared or not); frequency penalty instead grows with repeat count — the exam's confused-pair distinction between the two penalty parameters.

items.label: Generation should end the instant the model writes a specific marker string, without waiting to hit the length ceiling
items.why: A stop sequence is a literal string trigger that halts generation early; max_tokens only enforces a length ceiling and has no awareness of specific text.

items.label: A specific piece of text the model is told to treat as an ending marker, so output stops the moment that text is produced
items.why: Stop sequences trigger on matching text content; neither max_tokens nor frequency penalty inspects the generated text itself — one counts tokens, the other counts repeats.

items.label: Latency must stay predictable at high, sustained request volume, and the team is fine paying reserved hourly cost to guarantee it
items.why: Provisioned throughput (PTU) reserves dedicated capacity for predictable latency at scale; Standard deployment is pay-per-token with variable throughput under load, and Capacity (TPM) is only the quota dial, not the deployment type itself.

items.label: Reserved, dedicated model capacity purchased ahead of time so throughput does not fluctuate with shared-tenant traffic
items.why: PTU is the reserved-capacity deployment model; Standard shares capacity and bills per token with variable throughput, while Capacity (TPM) merely sets the quota on whichever deployment type is chosen.

items.label: Traffic to the customer-support app is unpredictable and bursty, and the team wants pay-per-token billing instead of hourly reserved capacity
items.why: Pay-per-token pricing under variable load is Standard deployment (the exam's exact scenario); PTU instead bills hourly for reserved capacity regardless of actual usage.

items.label: Bills per token consumed rather than per hour of reserved compute, with throughput that can vary under shared load
items.why: Standard is consumption-based billing with variable throughput; PTU trades that variability for a fixed hourly reservation, and Capacity (TPM) is the quota setting layered on top of either model.

items.label: A deployment keeps hitting throttling under peak load, so the team shifts spare throughput quota over from another underused deployment
items.why: The per-deployment throughput quota can be reallocated between deployments (the exam's documented scenario); PTU and Standard describe the deployment's billing/reservation model, not its quota dial.

items.label: The dial that sets an upper bound on total throughput a deployment can process each minute, independent of any single response's length
items.why: Capacity (TPM) throttles at the deployment level across all requests measured in tokens per minute; max_tokens instead caps the length of one response and has nothing to do with rate limiting.

items.label: The banner image request keeps returning a small square when the layout needs a wide rectangular canvas
items.why: size sets the pixel dimensions (e.g. a wide format instead of 1024x1024); quality controls rendering fidelity and n controls image count — neither changes the canvas shape.

items.label: The request field that sets the pixel dimensions of the generated image, such as 1024×1024
items.why: size is the dimensions field in the images/generations payload; quality instead governs rendering fidelity, and partial_images controls progressive streaming, not the final canvas dimensions.

items.label: The field that accepts the 'high' fidelity tier so fine detail renders more crisply, separate from how big the image is
items.why: quality (including the documented 'high' trap value) controls rendering fidelity; size controls dimensions and n controls how many images come back — three independent dials on the same request.

items.label: One prompt should return four separate image variations to choose between, in a single request
items.why: n sets how many images the request returns (e.g. n=4); size and quality shape each individual image but do not change how many come back.

items.label: The parameter that sets how many image variations a single images/generations call returns
items.why: n is the image-count field; partial_images instead streams progressive previews of a single image as it renders, and size only sets that image's dimensions.

items.label: Combined with streaming, this field sets how many progressive preview frames are sent before the final image completes
items.why: partial_images (used together with stream=True) sets the count of progressive preview frames during rendering; n instead sets how many separate final images are returned, and quality sets fidelity, not preview cadence.
